text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered -> PD-INC-8423: inference-gateway.euw1 5xx-rate spike (window=60s, 5xx_rate=7.8%)
pagerbot: autopager: firing rotation -> michael (primary oncall) :rotating_light:
michael (oncall): acked via PagerDuty, looking now. Can someone dump upstream error distribution?
sre-liz: looking at request traces — errors are 502/503 coming from inference-proxy -> model-side 504 timeouts and some 503s from the edge LB. Error traces show increased backend queueing.
devon: stack traces + logs show repeated kv-cache evictions around the same time: "kvcache: eviction_rate=0.42, miss_rate jump". Could be a cascade when many clients hit long context requests.
ops-jen: scaling up dedicated inference pool (eu-west) now, adding 6 replicas to inference-service. Running:```bash
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-service --replicas=18
# waiting 60s for pods
```
michael (oncall): good. Oncall runbook step1: confirm customer impact. Any app-level 5xx latency seen?
sre-liz: yes, some customers hitting prolonged 5xx on /v1/generate with sequence lengths > 1600 tokens. Traffic weight to eu-west is ~38% across customers.
alex: implementing quick routing fallback: switching heavy customers to a smaller-model-variant that uses shorter contexts. Doing a routing change in the gateway:```json
{ "route": "customer-heavy", "action": "route-to", "target": "model-small-v2" }
```
devon: also toggling aggressive prefix-kv cache warming off (it seems to thrash on these long requests). Patch to runtime suggested: set `prefetch.kv_warmup=false` on the pool. Pushing change to edge config now.
michael (oncall): plan: 1) scale replicas (ops-jen) 2) route heavy customers to model-small-v2 (alex) 3) disable kv warmup to avoid eviction storms (devon) 4) monitor 5xx rate and customer errors -> update PD when stable.
ops-jen: scale is in progress, pods are spinning and readiness probes passing. 503s dropping in the last 30s from 7.8% -> 3.2%.
incident-bot: alert update: PD-INC-8423 -> severity remains P1 until 5xx < 1% for 5m.
sre-liz: I see 503s trending down, but one AZ still showing higher latency on connections to CUDA hosts — maybe kernel-level memory pressure. I've flagged the nodepool; requesting an immediate evict + replace for two suspect nodes.
michael (oncall): do it. Use the prepared node-replace script.```bash
./infra/tools/evict-node --zone=euw1-b --label=evict-candidate
```
alex: routing change applied for three large customers (customer ids redacted). They report degraded quality but functional. No new 5xx from their clients.
devon: disabled kv warmup flag on the pool and restarted sidecars. Eviction rate dropped to normal. 5xx now at 0.6% over the last 60s.
michael (oncall): great. I'm marking incident as "mitigated" for customer-facing impact. Will keep thread open until PD auto-ack threshold passes. Please add any actions for follow-up.
ops-jen: recorded the scale and node replacements in the event log: infra-ticket INF-1129.
sre-liz: follow-up action items: 1) add rate-limited prefetch (avoid full warmup), 2) add model-variant autoscale for long-context jobs, 3) add alert to catch kv-eviction bursts earlier.
michael (oncall): agreed. I'll file the post-incident task list and assign owners. Also scheduling a postmortem with infra+runtime next weekday.
pagerbot: pager update: PD-INC-8423 -> Acknowledged by michael, status: mitigated -> monitoring.
incident-bot: customer-impact note: partial service degradation for subset of customers (long-context generation) for ~14 minutes, failover to smaller models applied.
michael (oncall): closing loop: if 5xx stays <1% for 10m, I'll close the PD. Thanks everyone. :+1:
alex: FYI saved the gateway routing diff in PR #4857 for audit.
ops-jen: infra ticket INF-1129 contains node IDs and logs.
sre-liz: I'll draft the postmortem and include the timing of cache evictions and the kernel OOM indicators.
michael (oncall): nice run. Moving to follow-up items.
